producer_report.summary: Answered review 2 in the squash-chain design with a documentation-only change; no code or tests changed. The design gets an Appendix B with a disposition for R2-M1, R2-m1, R2-m2, R2-m3, R2-n1 and R2-n2. §4.1, §4.2 step 1, §4.3, §4.6, §5 and §6 are revised to match. R2-M1: the core derives previous_job as the latest landed job in the base commit's history. A hand change or records-only commit does not reset it, and an unlanded predecessor is not named, so that chain is refused. When none is found the field is absent. This is stated as an assumption the user may change. R2-m2: one remaining job is judged by the single-job rule. A landed predecessor is found by loading its JobFiles at P and matching its fingerprint to fingerprint(P; R). A /1 predecessor is accepted, and the two partly-landed cases are merged into two tests. R2-m1: noted that the existing merge message is what the user sees; no change to check. R2-m3: §5 names AnyRecord, the schema-name table and the consumers run.rs, store.rs and jobs.rs, and puts RecordSet::load in athena-gate. R2-n1: a rules change on the base branch is named in §4.6. R2-n2: the cited long lines in D69 and the v0 design are rewrapped. D69 is amended and stays proposed. The changelog, the v0 pointer and the enforcement pointer are updated. The review file is untouched, and the build is left as a separate later job.

checks_run.note: All tests passed, including the wording scan and the enforcement-map test.

open_issues: previous_job derivation and the merge-message handling are assumptions the user may change.
The exact way the core reads landed outcomes from base history must be confirmed by the build job.
The consumer list for AnyRecord::Candidate may be incomplete; the build job should search again.
The build is not done and is for a later job.
mistakes: I first wrote a malformed bold marker ('**(inferred** from') in §4.6 and fixed it before finishing.
learnings: The design's own tests of previous_job, line numbers and consumers come from review 2's reading; I did not re-measure them in the code.
